sm.text: Selling, general and administrative expenses primarily consist of (i) administrative costs, including compensation, and professional fees, (ii) fees related to the Company’s Sponsorship Sales and Service Representation Agreement, and (iii) sales and marketing costs. In addition, selling, general and administrative expenses includes allocations from MSG Knicks for certain support functions that are provided on a centralized basis and not historically recorded at the component level by MSG Knicks, such as expenses related to executive management, finance, legal, human resources, government affairs, information technology and corporate operating lease costs. Selling, general and administrative expenses generally do not fluctuate in line with changes in the Company’s revenues and direct operating expenses.

In addition, selling, general and administrative expenses includes allocations from MSG Knicks for certain support functions that are provided on a centralized basis and not historically recorded at the component level by MSG Knicks, such as expenses related to executive management, finance, legal, human resources, government affairs, information technology and corporate operating lease costs. tax.heading: Income taxes
tax.text:
See Note 14 to the combined financial statements included in “Part I — Item 1. Financial Statements” of this Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for a discussion of the Company’s income taxes. Income taxes recognized in the combined financial statements and resulting effective tax rates may not be reflective of the taxes that the Company expects to recognize in the future as a standalone entity.

Changes in laws and regulations have limited and in the future could further limit the availability of tax benefits or deductions that the Company expects to claim or otherwise increase the taxes imposed on the Company’s operations. For example, Section 162(m) of the U.S. Internal Revenue Code generally limits a publicly held corporation’s deduction for compensation paid to each covered employee to $1 million per year. Effective for our tax year beginning on July 1, 2027, Section 162(m) expands the definition of “covered employee” to include the five highest compensated employees for the taxable year other than our principal executive officer, principal financial officer, and the three highest compensated executive officers. This expanded provision will apply to players on the Rangers, and would cause a significant amount of compensation expense to be nondeductible in Fiscal Year 2028 and beyond.

net.text: Adjusted operating income (loss) should be viewed as a supplement to and not a substitute for operating income (loss), net income (loss), cash flows from operating activities, and other measures of performance and/or liquidity presented in accordance with GAAP. Since adjusted operating income (loss) is not a measure of performance calculated in accordance with GAAP, this measure may not be comparable to similar measures with similar titles used by other companies. The Company has presented the components that reconcile operating income (loss), the most directly comparable GAAP financial measure, to adjusted operating income (loss).

ocf.heading: Operating Activities
ocf.text: Net cash used in operating activities for the three months ended September 30, 2026 increased by $66,077 to $71,188. The increase was primarily due to changes in working capital assets and liabilities, and to a lesser extent, the change in net loss adjusted for non-cash items. The changes in working capital assets and liabilities were primarily driven by (i) a higher decrease in accrued and other liabilities of $30,282, primarily due to higher payments related to league revenue sharing in the current year period, and (ii) a higher increase in net related party receivables of $25,163, primarily related to the timing of receipts under the Arena License Agreement and Sponsorship Sales & Service Agreement in the current year period.

intro.text: MSG Rangers Corp. (MSG Rangers) is a leading professional sports company, with a collection of assets that includes the New York Rangers (NHL) and a development league team, the Hartford Wolf Pack (AHL). MSG Rangers also operates a professional sports team performance center, the MSG Training Center in Greenburgh, NY. More information is available at msgrangers.com.
